# Networking Without Fear {#sec-networking-without-fear}

{{< credits 03-networking-without-fear >}}

::: {.callout-important}
## Draft
This chapter is an outline. Want to help write it? Start with @sec-your-first-contribution.
:::

## Goal

Understand your home network before installing anything.

## The big idea

IP addresses, the router, DHCP, DNS, NAT and ports.

## Outline

- Your router is the post office for your house
- IP addresses as street addresses
- DHCP hands out addresses, and why the server needs a fixed one
- DNS as the phone book of the internet
- Finding devices on your network
- Public vs private IPs and NAT: why the outside world can't reach your devices by default
- Ports as apartment numbers on the same street address

::: {.callout-note}
## Concept box: Why hotel Wi-Fi pops up a login page
Hotel networks intercept your first web request and redirect it to a sign-in page. Once you understand DNS and routers, that trick stops being mysterious.
:::

::: {.callout-warning}
## Break it on purpose
Give a device the wrong DNS server and see which sites fail.
:::
